complete-call.reason: Complete two-argument first-order call consumes one owner, X changes zero to one; ordinary Unit is explicitly supplied.

partial-call.reason: Missing Unit argument cannot create a reusable callable that captures q. No claim about an unimplemented closure grammar.

ordinary-local-callee.reason: The lexical ordinary Bit gate shadows the declaration; call lookup must not retry the global.

quantum-unit-tuple-callee.reason: A tuple carrying Q<Unit> remains linear data rather than a callable; zero width supplies no capture exception. The other declaration illustrates an explicit legal move only.

quantum-unit-tuple-provider.reason: The runtime tuple cannot supply an Op<Unit>; hidden owner/provider capture must reject before a concrete emitter may be selected.

static-description-reuse.reason: Reusing a closed then_op(X,X) description is allowed. Each application receives a different owner; X squared is exact identity on each.

owner-duplication.reason: The first application consumes q; a second use of the original owner is forbidden despite reusable static descriptions.

classical-condition.reason: Ordinary Bit selects one runtime branch; each branch returns the same input owner. b=1 chooses X.

quantum-condition.reason: Unmeasured Q<Bit> is not an ordinary Bit condition; branch syntax cannot observe it implicitly.

explicit-observation.reason: Explicit measure_z consumes the prepared |1> owner and yields ordinary Bit one; ordinary branch then returns zero.

limits: Stage/fragments predicted; no general closure/function/capture theorem or source/runtime preservation claim.
